ledger.event: F36 returned at 5c8f2ce and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED, on the same defect for the third time in two lanes: an assertion satisfied by construction. The compression claim built its expected line by calling firstSentence and ruleNamesACheck, the same two functions trapsDigest calls to build the line being compared, so it pinned a ternary and nothing else; the reviewer gutted compression twice with one-line mutations and the gate stayed green, once turning compression off entirely at 12261 bytes and once truncating all seventy-one rows to 6923. The object-resolves claim had no vacuity guard where its sibling did, so setting every object to star made it vanish silently. The lane's substance is good and confirmed at the objects: 71 objects with 19 non-star all resolving and 52 star rows judged honest against their rule text, no stored rule edited, no digest row dropped, and F31's prefix byte-identical across two lanes with the envelope still last, which is what D-58 deferred the scoping half to protect. Correction 1 issued, narrower than the first envelope: traps.yaml is finished and withheld, and the correction may not write an assertion in terms of the functions that produce what it asserts.

F36 landed from writer/F36 at b106bd2, fast-forward, after one correction. Four checks, each driven red by the control plane and again by the reviewer on faithful mutations: a recipe that hands the packet over as an argv string, a Windows line that takes the key from a bare env rather than the user store, a disjointReport whose overlap is always empty, and a census that ignores its injected lister. F39 issued at base 9934c6c, alone, and it takes the last two open sparks that have lanes. Five claims about the GitHub writer Action, each naming the mutation that must turn its check red. It becomes opt-in and idle by default, gated on a repository variable, because today issuing any lane fires a headless cloud seat onto writer/<LANE>, the branch a local worktree may already hold; on F33 exactly that happened and a stale key stopped it rather than design, which is S14. It takes the router instead of hardcoding DashScope and its own model table, so the cloud seat can reach the native path D-51 made default, and the secret it counts becomes the secret the call passes, which is S15 and which today turns T55's loud skip into a loud failure. A missing secret exits 0 with a reason. And the packet reaches it on stdin rather than as an argv string, which is T72 in the cloud path, surviving only because the runner is Linux. factory/tools/route.mjs is handed to the lane for its duration and the envelope says so rather than doing it silently; the router's answer does not change, only a second caller gains the ability to ask it.

F39 returned at 512e86b: CORRECTIONS NEEDED, and the defect is a new variant of the one D-59 names. F35 returned at 3c1dd95 and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED on the boundary the envelope told it to look hardest at. splitCheck takes the first case-insensitive match of check is or check colon, so ordinary prose beats the real directive: a row reading Confirm the box, then lowercase check is ticked before merge, then the real Check is node factory/tools/kitCheck.mjs --self-test, emits a rule of Confirm the box Confirm the box and a check of ticked before merge, always, with the real directive glued to the end. Driven at the objects through alumni.mjs intakes on a fixture tree, and that candidate clears the twelve-character floor and passes intake.mjs unedited, which is worse than being held because the owner acts on it. The same root cause has an inverse the printed list cannot distinguish: a false hit early in a row pushes the rule under its floor and a row with a good check is held as if it had none. Correction 1 makes the match case-sensitive and last-wins, with a fixture for each half. It also guards the module's dispatch, because node -e importing alumni.mjs prints the whole check pack, which is T14 latent and the same hazard F36 fixed in packet.mjs. What the review confirmed good and is not being touched: 75 rows read from this repository's own traps.yaml with 19 named and 56 held, every one of the 19 passing the gate unedited, read-only proved by a tree sha1 before and after a real run, and contracts/intake.v1.json correctly left alone because intake.mjs hardcodes its own key list and would refuse a new field.

What the review cleared: sameModel is symmetric and transitive as equality over a canonical form, the deepseek-v4-pro fold is deliberate and the router never sends the bare unversioned id to DashScope so T48's price collision is unreachable, an absent or empty model is refused before record() is entered, T65's read-first key holds live, and returns.json is untouched.
